record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Prove Arnold diffusion in general a priori stable systems, including those arising from celestial mechanics.

evidence.quote: Using Dyson equation for classical mechanics, Arnold diffusion can be proved in certain a priori stable systems [GGM], but the same question is open in general a priori stable systems such as those arising from celestial mechanics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H_0:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth strictly convex Hamiltonian depending only on the action variables $I\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and consider the nearly integrable Hamiltonian
\[ H_\varepsilon(I,\varphi) = H_0(I) + \varepsilon P(I,\varphi), \qquad (I,\varphi)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{T}^n, \]
with $n\ge 3$ and $P$ a generic smooth (or real-analytic) perturbation. Such a system is called a priori stable, since for $\varepsilon=0$ the entire phase space is foliated by invariant Lagrangian tori carrying quasi-periodic motions.

Arnold diffusion refers to the existence, for arbitrarily small $\varepsilon\ne 0$, of orbits $(I(t),\varphi(t))$ of $H_\varepsilon$ along which the action variable $I(t)$ undergoes a displacement of order one:
\[ \|I(T) - I(0)\| \ge \delta, \]
for some $\delta>0$ independent of $\varepsilon$ and some time $T=T(\varepsilon)$.

Problem. Prove that Arnold diffusion occurs generically in a priori stable Hamiltonian systems with $n\ge 3$ degrees of freedom, including those arising from celestial mechanics such as the planetary $N$-body problem and the spatial restricted three-body problem in regimes where the unperturbed system is properly degenerate but stable.
artifact.status_search_result: Arnold diffusion has been established in various a priori unstable settings and in some specific a priori stable models (notably for cusp-residual perturbations in three degrees of freedom by Cheng, Kaloshin–Zhang, and others), but the general case of a priori stable systems—particularly those of celestial-mechanics origin such as the planetary N-body problem—remains open. Recent (2024–2025) work proves Arnold diffusion in concrete restricted three-body settings and degenerate models, but does not resolve the general problem.

status_evidence.title: Arnold Diffusion in the Full Three-Body Problem
status_evidence.snippet: The full three-body problem is one of the oldest unsolved problems in classical mechanics; recent work establishes Arnold diffusion in specific cases.
status_evidence.claim: Arnold diffusion is established only in specific celestial-mechanics models, not in the general a priori stable setting.

status_evidence.title: A degenerate Arnold diffusion mechanism in the restricted 3-body problem
status_evidence.snippet: Extending a priori unstable results to the a priori stable case displays many features that remain challenging; results in the smooth category for 3 d.o.f. have not been extended to real-analytic a priori stable Hamiltonians.
status_evidence.claim: The general a priori stable case, including degenerate celestial-mechanics systems, is still open.

status_evidence.title: On the Arnold Diffusion Mechanism in Medium Earth Orbit
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work examines Arnold diffusion mechanisms in concrete celestial-mechanics applications such as medium Earth orbit.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on Arnold diffusion in celestial mechanics, indicating the general problem is not closed.
